clue.text: Arab standing by arches in the gym?

definitions.text: Arab standing by arches in the gym?

indicators.note: standing by places the Arab next to the word for arches

parts.note: vaulting is the arched work of a roof or ceiling, its arches taken together
an Arab is a breed of riding animal, a steed

explanation.surface: An Arab man waits beside some archways inside a gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a whimsical description of the gym apparatus, while 'standing by' also sets the Arab (a steed) beside a word for arches.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the padded gym apparatus that athletes leap over is named as if it were a steed beside arched roofing.

clue.text: University administrator briefly displaying miniature Victoria Cross

parts.note: written in short the title is VC, the same two letters that abbreviate the Victoria Cross, Britain's highest medal for gallantry

explanation.surface: A senior academic shows off a tiny replica of a gallantry medal for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' asks for the title's abbreviation, which is VC; that is also the short form of the Victoria Cross, Britain's highest military decoration, so the abbreviated official 'displays' a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: Job title: in British universities this officer is the working head who runs the institution.

clue.text: Perfect state?

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, complete or absolute, as in a perfect stranger
as a verb, to say or declare something

explanation.definitionFit: Two synonyms: an adjective meaning complete or absolute, and a verb meaning to say or declare.

clue.text: Worried Tories adopt member with hesitation — he procrastinates

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the jumbled letters take the member inside them
worried means disturbed or agitated, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Anxious Conservatives reluctantly select a candidate who then puts everything off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' gives the jumble TEORIS, and 'adopt' is the insertion signal. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, so the surface is a candidate selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent noun: someone who delays and stalls to gain time is one who puts things off.

clue.text: Give an account of charge incurred in the first place

indicators.note: in the first place tells you the piece from incurred goes at the start, ahead of the charge

parts.note: to incur a debt is to run it up; 'ran up', taken literally in a down entry, is RAN written upwards
a rate is a charge or price, as in a daily rate

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to explain a fee that was run up originally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incurred' has to be read as 'ran up', and this is a down entry, so RAN is written upwards as NAR; 'in the first place' sets it ahead of RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tell or relate a story is to recount what happened.

clue.text: Man introducing prohibition in north-east plant

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man, and introducing only says it comes ahead of the rest

indicators.note: in places the prohibition inside the compass point

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A man brings a ban on alcohol to a factory in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'plant' to be a factory in north-east England; it is a poisonous herb. 'in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a poisonous flowering herb of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Woodland path where Lucy Ashton lost her head

indicators.note: losing her head means the word for Lucy drops its first letter

parts.note: Lucy Ashton is the title character of Walter Scott's novel The Bride of Lammermoor

explanation.surface: A track through the trees is where a Scott heroine went mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucy Ashton is the bride in Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor, who does go mad in the story; 'lost her head' removes the first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: a track cut through a wood for people on horseback.

clue.text: Ten operas translated into Zamenhof's language

indicators.note: translated means carried into another form, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten operas are put into the tongue that Zamenhof invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the ten letters of TEN OPERAS. L. L. Zamenhof was the Polish doctor who devised this artificial international tongue in 1887.
explanation.definitionFit: Identification: Zamenhof created this constructed international tongue.

clue.text: Presumptuous young man, aggressive physically and verbally?

parts.note: one who attacks with a lash is a whipper
one who is aggressive in speech snaps at people, so is a snapper

explanation.surface: A cheeky youth who is hostile both with his fists and with his tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: the word is split into one who lashes and one who speaks sharply, the 'aggressive' applying to both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an impertinent, cheeky youngster who thinks too much of himself.

clue.text: Boat in river, carrying volunteers to islands

indicators.note: carrying means the river holds the volunteers inside it

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A vessel on a river ferries helpers out to some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the insertion signal. The volunteers are the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force; the river flows through Cambridge and the islands lie off western Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a twin-hulled sailing vessel.

clue.text: The wisdom of such a charge?

definitions.meaning: the word goes before 'charge' to name the underwater explosive dropped on submarines

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for profundity of thought, and the word that precedes 'charge' in the name of an anti-submarine explosive.

clue.text: Rare object seen about university city

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, is known as Rio

explanation.surface: An unusual item is spotted somewhere around a university town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'university city' together as one place; the two words are separate pieces, and 'about' is not a container but the abbreviation of circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unusual or intriguing collectable item.

clue.text: The first man Jarndyce's ward married

parts.note: Ada Clare is a ward of John Jarndyce in Dickens's Bleak House

explanation.surface: The first suitor that the ward of Mr Jarndyce took as a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Ada Clare is one of John Jarndyce's wards in Dickens's novel Bleak House.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical identification: in Genesis he is the earliest human created.

clue.text: Stock of pigs rejected, but not in Wodehouse's ending

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so what remains is read backwards
but not tells you the letters that follow are left out of the word for of pigs

parts.note: porcine means of or relating to pigs
taken as written

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of the author's name

explanation.surface: A farmer's pigs are turned down, though not in the last pages of a Wodehouse novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes three letters, leaving PORC, which 'rejected' turns round; 'ending' picks the author's last letter. P. G. Wodehouse's comic novels feature a prize pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared sense: both words name the handle of a whip, and a short riding whip.

clue.text: It may indicate possession of an address

definitions.meaning: the punctuation mark written before an s to show ownership
in rhetoric, a speech turned to an absent person or a personified thing

explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark showing ownership, and the rhetorical figure of speaking to someone absent.

clue.text: Obtain a hundred and four folded sheets of paper

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quire was originally four sheets of paper folded to make eight leaves

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of a hundred and four creased pages.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a hundred and four' as one number, 104; it splits into A, the Roman numeral C, and then four folded sheets, the original meaning of QUIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to get or come to possess something.

clue.text: Prompt measure taken by dancers

parts.note: prompt means quick, done without delay
a step is a measure, as in taking steps to deal with something

explanation.surface: A dance troupe acts fast to deal with a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the dance, a 'measure' being an old word for a dance, while its first two words also give the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a fast ballroom dance, 'measure' being an old word for a dance.

clue.text: Sweep the area

definitions.meaning: a broad unbroken stretch, as in a sweep of moorland
a wide extent of space or surface

explanation.definitionFit: Both are synonyms for a wide open stretch of land or space.

clue.text: Each rim damaged? It's monstrous!

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Every wheel rim on the car has been dented, which is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the seven letters of EACH RIM. 'monstrous' is literal: this is the fire-breathing monster of Greek myth, part lion, part goat, part serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Greek myth it is a fire-breathing beast made of lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Be troubled after entering note in margin

indicators.note: entering means the word for after goes inside the word for be troubled

parts.note: to ail is to be troubled or unwell
post is the Latin prefix meaning after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: Someone frets once they have written a comment at the side of the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' looks like part of 'entering note', as if writing one down, but it is the insertion signal, and 'after' is a piece, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: a marginal annotation on a document.

clue.text: Utter oaths about a cat's habits

indicators.note: about means the word for swearing goes round the cat

parts.note: to cuss is to swear
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone swears loudly at the things a cat regularly does.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Utter' as an adjective; it is the verb in a phrase for swearing, which 'about' wraps round the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the usual practices of a person or a people.

clue.text: Misrepresents the national flag

definitions.meaning: as a verb, gives a distorted slant to facts or a report
the flag of a country, ship or regiment, as in saluting it

explanation.surface: Someone gives a false picture of the country's banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning distorts or slants an account, and a plural noun for a country's or regiment's banner.

clue.text: Liberal president, so to speak

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A president who is, as it were, on the progressive side.
explanation.walkthrough: Ike was the nickname of Dwight D. Eisenhower, US president from 1953 to 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial filler: both are dropped into speech to mean 'as it were'.

clue.text: Minion gets plunder in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the word for plunder is read from its end

parts.note: loot is plunder, stolen goods

explanation.surface: A henchman grabs spoils as the army falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns LOOT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a person used by another to do their bidding.

clue.text: Game doctor has a dance

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the fifteen-a-side game
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A sporting medic takes a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union, a British staple of crosswords, and MB is the medical degree Bachelor of Medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rhythmic ballroom style of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Two mothers thus formally addressed

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A pair of mums are spoken to in very polite terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' points back at the wordplay: the two mothers set side by side spell the polite form used to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: it is the polite title used when speaking to a woman.

clue.text: Raised money in an audience

indicators.note: an audience is a hearing, so the word for money is heard rather than read

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds are collected from the people at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in an audience' asks for a word that sounds like BREAD, slang for money. The surface reads 'Raised money' as fundraising; only 'Raised' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: brought up or reared, as children or livestock are.

clue.text: Fish-eater appearing in Holy Writ three times

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible
ter is Latin for three times, used on prescriptions and in music

explanation.surface: A creature that lives on fish turns up in the Bible on three occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ter' is Latin for thrice, seen on prescriptions (ter in die) and in musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a river mammal that lives chiefly on what it catches in the water.

clue.text: Phoney parliament defended by fellow at university

indicators.note: defended by means the parliament is shielded on both sides by the fellow

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, standing for a fellow
the Rump was the remnant of the English Parliament left after Pride's Purge of 1648
in British usage a student who is up is in residence at university

explanation.surface: A sham assembly is stood up for by a don at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defended by' is the insertion signal. The parliament is the remnant English one left after Pride's Purge in 1648, and in British usage a student in residence at university is 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fabricated or invented, as false charges are.

clue.text: Confuses players coming in by ship

indicators.note: coming in means the two pieces before it go inside the word for by

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
to addle is to muddle or confuse
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Bewildered sportsmen arrive by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by ship' reads as one phrase but splits: 'by' is the outer piece that 'coming in' fills, and 'ship' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a vessel driven by revolving wheels and a boiler.
